theorem: Let A,B>=0 and X>=0 in arbitrary finite bipartite dimensions. Suppose the whitened operator Y=(A^(1/2) tensor B^(1/2))^+ X (A^(1/2) tensor B^(1/2))^+ is maximally correlated in some local orthonormal bases, meaning Y=sum_ij c_ij |u_i v_i><u_j v_j| with C=(c_ij)>=0. Then W=A tensor B-X is product-block-positive if and only if W^Gamma>=0. In particular any 2-block-positive member is completely copositive and cannot detect a PPT state, even if X has arbitrary rank. This extends the single-negative-rank-one result in frontier-20261028-product-metric-witness-no-go-v1.json SHA256 276aa8338c8e431e6edba2c32f157ae06ff21bf2050698dd41d579e1991a6c65. No novelty is claimed.
singular_support: Let S=A^(1/2) tensor B^(1/2). Product-block-positivity evaluated at x tensor y with x in ker A gives <xy|X|xy>=0. Since X>=0 this implies X^(1/2)|xy>=0, so X annihilates ker A tensor the whole Bob space; similarly it annihilates the whole Alice space tensor ker B. Hence X is supported on ran A tensor ran B and X=S Y S^*. If either metric factor is zero, product-block-positivity forces X=0 and W=0.
copt_proof: Product-block-positivity of W transfers through the local pseudoinverse to I-Y on the support. Testing each basis product u_i tensor v_i gives 0<=c_ii<=1. Positivity of C gives |c_ij|^2<=c_ii*c_jj<=1. In the partial-transposed correlated basis, Y^Gamma has eigenvalues c_ii and pairs +/-|c_ij|, plus zeros; therefore Y^Gamma<=I. Local congruence yields W^Gamma=(A^(1/2) tensor conjugate(B^(1/2)))*(I-Y^Gamma)*(...)^*>=0, including singular metrics. The reverse implication follows immediately by testing W^Gamma on product vectors with conjugated Bob factor. For every PPT rho, tr(W rho)=tr(W^Gamma rho^Gamma)>=0. Local product congruences and nonnegative sums preserve coCP.
example: Set A=diag(1,4,0,9), B=diag(4,0,9,1), and choose correlated support kets |00>,|12>,|33> with C=[[1,1/2,0],[1/2,1,1/2],[0,1/2,1]]. C is PSD of rank3 with pivots (1,3/4,2/3), and W^Gamma is PSD. W itself is not PSD: x=(1/2)|00>+(1/3)|12>+(1/3)|33> gives <x|W|x>=-4. The rank2 vector y=(1/2)|00>+(1/6)|12> gives -1, so this example is NOT 2-block-positive; its role is to demonstrate that coCP need not mean PSD. The preceding single-rank-one artifact gives a genuine 2-block-positive non-PSD example.

exact_check.observed: Fraction arithmetic checks the rank3 correlated matrix PSD, all256 entries of W and its PT, nonnegative PT Schur pivots, and the exact -4 and -1 test expectations. The universal conclusion is the written support, 2x2 coefficient-minor and partial-transpose block proof.

limits: The positive offset is a single product metric and the whitened positive subtraction is maximally correlated in a common local basis. General noncorrelated subtractions, nonproduct offsets, all 2-positive maps, unrestricted 4x4 PPT states, novelty and external/formal review remain open.
